text.title: Roadmap Design Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding Roadmap Design. Each pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale; HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override.

rule.statement: Each roadmap item is an outcome statement, not a feature. Features sit beneath outcomes.
rule.rationale: Each roadmap item is an outcome statement, not a feature. Features sit beneath outcomes.

rule.statement: Use Now / Next / Later horizons; do not put dates on Next or Later.
rule.rationale: Use Now / Next / Later horizons; do not put dates on Next or Later.

rule.statement: Every item carries a confidence label (high/medium/low) tied to evidence held.
rule.rationale: Every item carries a confidence label (high/medium/low) tied to evidence held.

rule.statement: Roadmap reviewed quarterly; items can move between horizons or off.
rule.rationale: Roadmap reviewed quarterly; items can move between horizons or off.

rule.statement: Later items are bets, not commitments; copy must read that way.
rule.rationale: Later items are bets, not commitments; copy must read that way.

rule.statement: Select the format from the uncertainty level before applying r2: low → timeline (or Kanban when the audience is internal only); medium → Now/Next/Later; high → outcome-themed, or Now/Next/Later at theme level when it is shared externally. r2's horizon rules bind once Now/Next/Later is the selected format.
rule.rationale: Format mismatch is the root cause of roadmap trust failures — a timeline in a high-uncertainty context creates commitments that cannot be kept, and stakeholder trust dies on the first slip. Uncertainty and the external-sharing requirement pick the format; audience preference does not, because stakeholders always ask for dates.

rule.statement: Maintain one internal source-of-truth roadmap; emit every external view as a derivative of it — never copy-paste.
rule.rationale: Two hand-maintained copies diverge within one cycle, and the copy the customer holds is the one nobody re-checks. A derived view cannot drift from its source.

rule.statement: The external view names themes and benefits only — never specific metric targets, confidence labels, or owners.
rule.rationale: A published metric target is read as a commitment and creates contractual expectation; a published confidence label is read as incompetence. Each audience needs a different abstraction level.

rule.statement: Internal roadmap: monthly review. External roadmap: quarterly publish. Both cadences are named in the artefact, not left implicit.
rule.rationale: r4 fixes the review beat; this fixes the publish beat. A roadmap reviewed monthly but never republished leaves stakeholders reading a stale external view while the team believes it is current.

rule.statement: Every roadmap carries an explicit not-doing list at the horizon scope, each entry with a reason.
rule.rationale: Without stated exclusions every reasonable idea stays a candidate for this quarter. The list doubles as a review log that closes re-requests with a reference instead of reopening the debate.

rule.statement: If preconditions in AGENTS.md "Applies If" do not all hold, OR any "Skip If" disqualifier is true, do not run this methodology — route to the named alternative.
rule.rationale: Methodologies are pre-condition gated; running them out-of-scope produces noise and burns the agent context budget.

rule.statement: If preconditions hold, execute the procedure in `content/04-procedure.xml` (or the rule set above when complexity is light), emit the artefact specified by `content/02-output-contract.xml`, and validate with `scripts/validate-roadmap-design.py` before returning.
rule.rationale: Tying the entry rule to the validator script closes the loop between policy and machine check.
